title: Trust and safety
description: Review how the product prevents, detects and handles abuse, illegal content and harmful behaviour by its users, and how affected people can report and appeal.
expertises: Notice and action, statements of reasons and appeals
questions: What could a user publish, send or do with this change that harms another person or breaks the law?
How does someone report it, who reviews the report and how fast?
How is the affected user told about a decision, and how can they contest it?

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2021/784 on addressing the dissemination of terrorist content online
The Santa Clara Principles on Transparency and Accountability in Content Moderation
Digital Trust & Safety Partnership, Best Practices Framework

specialists.title: Abuse risk analyst
specialists.focus: List how the change could be misused: spam, fraud, harassment, illegal content, impersonation or evasion of a ban, and estimate the scale.
checks: Each new way to publish, message or invite is listed with the abuse it enables.
Rate limits and verification steps are defined for new accounts and bulk actions.
The risk assessment is dated and reviewed when the feature changes.

specialists.title: Moderation operations lead
specialists.focus: Design the reporting flow, the review queue, the response times and the escalation for urgent cases such as threats to life or child safety.
checks: Any user, logged in or not, can report content with a reason and a location in the product.
Urgent categories have a separate queue, a response target and an on-call owner.
Removal orders from authorities for terrorist content can be handled within one hour, as Regulation (EU) 2021/784 requires of hosting services.

specialists.title: Policy and appeals specialist
specialists.focus: Write the rule the decision applies, the statement of reasons sent to the affected user and the appeal path reviewed by a different person.
checks: Every action on content or an account cites the rule it applies.
The affected user receives a statement of reasons with the facts, the rule and how to appeal.
Appeals are reviewed by someone not involved in the first decision, and reinstatements are counted.

specialists.title: Transparency and regulatory reporting lead
specialists.focus: Check which reporting obligations apply, such as Digital Services Act transparency reports, and that the data needed to produce them is recorded.
checks: Notices, actions, appeals and response times are recorded in a form that can be counted.
Automated moderation is identified as such in the records and its error rate is sampled by people.
The service's status under the Digital Services Act, or other applicable law, is confirmed with legal.

evidence: Abuse risk assessment for the change, with the scenarios and their mitigations.
Reporting flow, moderation queue design and response time targets.
Policy text, statement of reasons template and appeal procedure.
Current moderation metrics: reports, actions, appeals, reinstatements and response times.
challenge: How would a determined abuser use this feature at scale, and what stops them?
What happens to a report sent on a Saturday night about a threat to someone's safety?
Could automated moderation remove lawful content without a person able to reverse it?
Does the policy say clearly enough what is not allowed for a user to understand a decision?
decision_criteria: Proceed when abuse scenarios have mitigations, reports reach a staffed queue and users receive reasons and an appeal.
Revise when a new way to publish or message ships without reporting, rate limits or a review queue.
Block when the service cannot meet a legal removal or reporting deadline that applies to it, until legal confirms the plan.
Name the safety metrics, such as response time to urgent reports and appeal reversal rate, and their thresholds.
